questions_provoked: Q1 scope — "network diagram, wan down to the db": the whole path (WAN, firewall, core, then the web/Redis/DB tiers), or just one edge of it?
Q2 reader's job — what do you read off it: the link speeds, which application talks to which, or just the box layout?
Q3 shape — one pane beside the chat, or a canvas I can pan?
Q4 motion — are the dots a measurement? Should a 25 GbE link show faster dots than a 1 GbE one?
Q5 Redis — the ask names WAN and the db but not Redis: does the 25 GbE core link and the web-to-Redis session both stay, or does Redis fold into the web tier?
Q6 dots on every line, or only some — should the three application relations (session, queries, fill) carry dots too, or only the transport links?
Q7 qualifiers — do the historical speed facts stay printed on the links even where a link is not exercised?

questions_used.question: Q1 scope — the whole path, or just the edge?
questions_used.answer: WAN through firewall and core, down to web, Redis and the database. All of it.

questions_used.question: Q2 reader's job — link speeds, or the application pairing?
questions_used.answer: I need to read the link speeds and see which application talks to which — not a picture of the boxes.

questions_used.question: Q3 shape — one pane, or a canvas?
questions_used.answer: One pane, side-by-side. It's small enough.

questions_used.question: Q4 motion — is the dot speed a measurement?
questions_used.answer: No. Slow sparse dots show traffic direction; the GbE labels are the measurement. Never imply the dot speed is the link speed.

questions_used.question: Q5 Redis — does the 25 GbE core link and the web-to-Redis session both stay?
questions_used.answer: Both stay, as two separate relations: core->cache 25 GbE and web->cache session are distinct, and Redis is its own tier behind the core.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — source.md's Fixed constraints say "Preserve separate core-to-cache and web-to-cache relations" and the relationship facts list both; the annex is silent, so the source decides. No fact is added.

questions_used.question: Q6 dots on every line, or only the transport links?
questions_used.answer: Dots on the four directional transport links only (wan->fw, fw->core, core->web, core->cache); the three application relations stay static.
questions_used.answer_source: own judgment — source.md asks for "slow, sparse motion" and for dots whose "direction represents the flow of traffic", while TRIAGE-network-4 says the labels are the measurement and dot speed never is. Sparse plus that correction make the four speed-labelled hops the dotted set; all four run at the default constant 0.5 c/step so no dot can read as 1/10/25 GbE, and the static triangle leaves the session/queries/fill labels uncrowded. No annex answer covers the split; no node, relation or qualifier is introduced by it.

questions_used.question: Q7 qualifiers — do the historical speeds stay printed verbatim?
questions_used.answer: Yes: "1 GbE", "10 GbE", "10 GbE", "25 GbE" — the two 10 GbE links are separate edges, each keeping its own label.

engine_observations: In a3 the ownership repair could not place "session" unambiguously and reported 1 ambiguous owner with labels_leadered: 0 instead of falling back to a leader tick; a4 removed the cause geometrically.

In tb the engine sizes a rank gap from the *width* of an edge label (label_width + 3 rows) unless that edge sets label_slot, so a six-character speed label costs nine rows of height per gap. That is the dominant cost in this case (a1 29x67 -> a2 27x45).
